## Sketching tangent graphs {#fgt1-tangent .trig-lesson}

For $y=\textcolor{#b55224}{a}\tan \textcolor{#007f78}{n}x+\textcolor{#3b66a8}{k}$, the period is $T=\dfrac{\pi}{|\textcolor{#007f78}{n}|}$.

::: {.split}
::: {.column-block}
<h3>Asymptotes first</h3>

- Mark the centre $(0,\textcolor{#3b66a8}{k})$.
- Draw the nearest asymptotes at $x=\pm\dfrac{T}{2}$.
- Repeat the asymptotes every $T$ units.

:::
::: {.column-block}
<h3>Then each branch</h3>

- Use $T/4$ to locate guide points.
- Check the direction of the branch.
- Keep the branches separate.

:::
:::

::: {.takeaway .fragment}
Tangent has no amplitude. The coefficient $\textcolor{#b55224}{a}$ gives a vertical dilation and may also reflect the graph.
:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 14 · Example 1.13</p>

::: notes

a,n are nonzero. A tangent graph is unbounded: a vertical dilation factor is not an amplitude. For n>0 the central branch has guide points (−T/4,k−a),(0,k),(T/4,k+a); if n<0 its direction reverses. In general the branch increases when an>0 and decreases when an<0. The unshifted vertical asymptotes are x=(π/2+jπ)/n, j an integer; their spacing is T. Use j here to distinguish the integer index from the vertical translation k. Range is R. On a specified domain exclude every asymptote, including boundary values if applicable. This two-minute explanation prepares the next full sketch. Source reference is conceptual; no additional booklet task is assigned here.

:::
